operator_allow_list_source: Declared in scripts/export_benchmark_m6.py::ALLOWED_OPS, NOT derived from the graph it validates (KB Decision 51). GridSample and the mask's boolean ops are M6's additions over M5's census.

runtime_contract.encoder: structure(1,7,288,512) -> prev_features(1,480,36,64); run ONCE per frame
runtime_contract.cross_frame_state: prev_features (1,480,36,64) float — 1.11 MiB at fp32, 0.55 at fp16
runtime_contract.note: M10 CONSEQUENCE, recorded because no earlier rung needed it: the runtime must hold one feature tensor from the previous frame. The M5 runtime was stateless. Cold start (frame 0, or motion_valid false) passes no history and reduces Model D exactly to Model C.

latency_note: Batch 1, 288x512, TensorRT engine time only — CUDA events around execute_async_v3. EXCLUDES host<->device transfers, the structural export, Godot's frame cost and the cross-frame copy. Not an end-to-end FPS figure. The per-frame runtime cost is encoder + renderer, since the encoder runs once per frame to produce the NEXT frame's history.

trt_fp32.tolerance_note: EXCEEDS the 1e-3 tolerance (1.346e-03) and is recorded as exceeding it, not waived. Context, which is not a defence: the 1e-3 figure was written at M4 for a SIGMOID-BOUNDED [0,1] RGB output, and this stage emits UNBOUNDED encoder features (mean |x| 0.495, p99 1.623, max 3.111), so an absolute bound is the wrong instrument here - the deviation is 8.3e-04 of the p99 magnitude. The renderer stage, which does emit [0,1] RGB, passes at 1.65e-04. An intermediate-tensor stage needs its own RELATIVE tolerance before it can be gated; none is invented here, and none of M6's conclusions depend on this stage passing. KB Decision 59.

m5_comparison.note: M5's figure is a single one-input graph; M6's is encoder + renderer, because the history must be produced each frame. Compare FP32 to FP32 only — M6 has no FP16 engine here.

latency_finding.note: Model D costs 19.80 ms per frame in FP32 against Model C's 13.48 ms - a 47% increase, and at the TOP of §12's 15-20 ms StructFormer allocation. The cost is structural, not incidental: the encoder must run once per frame to produce the NEXT frame's history, so a temporal rung pays two graph executions where a frame-independent one pays one. NO FP16 ENGINE WAS BUILT for Model D, so the FP16 comparison against M5's 4.22 ms does not exist and must not be inferred - M5's FP16 needed a separately exported fp16 graph (Decision 45/48). This is a real deployment cost for a rung that did not pass its exit criterion.
